name: Non-syndromic Complete Hemimelia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Hemimelia

criteria.description: Complete absence of one or more bones along the longitudinal axis of a limb without associated syndromic features
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic conditions associated with limb deficiencies
Radiographic evidence confirming complete absence of the affected bone(s) in the limb
Normal karyotype and absence of chromosomal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete longitudinal absence of bone(s) in a limb confirmed radiologically, with exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing is used to exclude syndromic associations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete longitudinal absence of tibia or fibula
Unilateral limb length discrepancy due to bone absence
searchTerms: one leg shorter due to missing bone
unequal leg length from bone absence
limb length difference from missing bone

common.symptomName: Foot deformities including equinovarus or clubfoot

searchTerms: one leg shorter than the other

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in adjacent joints

searchTerms: small muscles in affected arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Compensatory scoliosis due to limb length discrepancy
searchTerms: spine curvature from leg length difference
uneven spine due to limb length
scoliosis caused by leg length mismatch

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue contractures around affected joints
searchTerms: restricted joint movement from tissue tightness

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb edema secondary to altered biomechanics
searchTerms: slight edema in affected arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones related to limb deficiency

searchTerms: hip joint abnormality on same side
hip socket problem with limb defect
wear and tear arthritis near affected joints
joint degeneration secondary to limb issues
nerve and vessel anomalies in arm or leg

imaging: X-ray showing complete absence of one or more long bones in a limb
MRI to assess soft tissue and muscle hypoplasia
genetic: No pathogenic variants associated with syndromic limb deficiencies
Negative for known mutations in syndromic hemimelia genes
other: Clinical examination confirming isolated limb deficiency without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with skin and soft tissue defects

redFlags: Presence of systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic association
Rapid progression of limb deformity postnatally
references: Hunter AGW, et al. Congenital Limb Deficiencies. In: Emery’s Elements of Medical Genetics. 15th ed. 2020.
